meta.title: mybackhurts: a tiny desk app that gets you off your chair
meta.description: mybackhurts is a tiny app for Mac and Windows that reminds you to get up every 45 minutes and walks you through two or three short exercises. It can count your reps with the webcam, on-device. Free, no account.
meta.ogTitle: mybackhurts: your back called, it wants a word
meta.ogDescription: A tiny app for Mac and Windows that gets you off your chair every 45 minutes. Reps counted on-device. No video leaves your computer. Free, no account.
meta.ogImageAlt: mybackhurts: “Your back called. It wants a word.” A stick figure slumped over a laptop at a desk says “ow.”

og.tagline1: A tiny app for Mac and Windows that gets you

hero.title:
Your back called.
It wants a word.
hero.lede: mybackhurts lives in your menu bar or system tray, nudges you every 45 minutes and walks you through a few quick moves. The camera stays off unless you ask it to count your reps.
hero.figureTitle: A stick figure slumped over a laptop, who sits up and stretches, then slumps again.

moves.title: Moves you can do next to your desk.
moves.subtitle: Office clothes and headphones welcome.

posture.label: Show the standing or seated moves

squat.name: Chair Squat
squat.figureTitle: A stick figure doing a chair squat.
squat.description: Sit back, tap the chair, stand tall.

calf.name: Standing Calf Raise
calf.figureTitle: A stick figure rising onto toes for a calf raise.
calf.description: Rise onto your toes, then lower slowly.

seatedCalf.name: Seated Calf Raise
seatedCalf.figureTitle: A stick figure on a stool lifting its heels.
seatedCalf.description: Heels up, heels down, without leaving your chair.

march.name: Standing March
march.figureTitle: A stick figure marching on the spot with its knees up high.
march.description: Knees up high, arms swinging, one side then the other.

seatedMarch.name: Seated March
seatedMarch.figureTitle: A stick figure on a stool lifting one knee, then the other.
seatedMarch.description: Sit tall and lift one knee, then the other.

arms.name: Arm Circles
arms.figureTitle: A stick figure drawing circles with both arms.
arms.description: Arms out, small circles, a little bigger each time.

chest.name: Chest Opener
chest.figureTitle: A stick figure raising its arms into a goalpost.
chest.description: Arms up like a goalpost, squeeze your shoulder blades, hold 20 seconds.

shrugs.name: Shoulder Shrugs
shrugs.figureTitle: A stick figure lifting and lowering both shoulders.
shrugs.description: Shoulders up to your ears, then let them drop.

neck.name: Neck Side Stretch
neck.figureTitle: A stick figure tilting its head for a neck side stretch.
neck.description: Ear to shoulder, 15 seconds each side.

wrist.name: Wrist & Forearm Stretch
wrist.figureTitle: A stick figure reaching one arm out and gently pulling its fingers back.
wrist.description: Arm out, fingers up, ease them back with the other hand. 15 seconds a side.

eye.name: 20-20-20 Eye Break
eye.figureTitle: A stick figure on a stool looking out of a far window.
eye.description: Look at something far away for 20 seconds. Blinking is allowed.

modes.title: Count your own reps, or let the camera count.
modes.simpleBody: A timer and a +1 rep button (or Space). The camera never turns on.
modes.webcamBody: An on-device pose model tracks your joints to count reps and holds, with form hints.

faq.title:
Things people
usually ask.
faq.scheduleQuestion: Will it bother me at 11pm on a Sunday?
faq.scheduleAnswer: Only if you say you work then. You pick the hours, days and interval.
faq.countingQuestion: How good is the rep counting?
faq.countingAnswer: Decent, not magic. Light and camera position matter, and calf raises often fall back to a timer. If the camera loses you, one click lets you count it yourself.
faq.officeQuestion: I'm in an open office. Will I look weird?
faq.officeAnswer: A little. Set posture to Seated and every break works from your chair.
faq.callQuestion: How does it know I'm on a call?
faq.callAnswer: It checks whether another app is using your camera or microphone, or is full screen. It never opens either one itself, so it never asks for permission.
